options.help: increase verbosity
options.detail: Repeat for more detail: -vv adds the limiting-stage estimate (reading, network or writing) to progress and to the final summary.

options.help: suppress non-error messages
options.detail: Suppresses progress, file lines and the dry-run plan. Errors and the end-of-run error summary still print.

options.help: skip based on checksum, not mod-time & size
options.detail: Both sides hash candidate files; progress shows verifying N checks. A content difference with matching size and time is reported as c in the change code.

options.help: archive mode; equals -rlptgoD
options.detail: Does not imply -H, -A, -X, -U, -N, -E or --fileflags. With --files-from, -a does not enable recursion; add -r.

options.help: recurse into directories
transfer directories without recursing
options.detail: Copies named directories without their contents. Implied by --files-from.

options.help: preserve source path components and implied directories
options.detail: A /./ component cuts off the prefix: xs -aR /data/./project/file dest/ creates dest/project/file. Implied directories get their source attributes. --no-implied-dirs still delegates to rsync.

options.help: select source names from FILE ("-" reads stdin)
options.detail: Names are relative to the single source directory. - reads stdin, :FILE reads the list on the remote machine of the transfer. Leading slashes refer to the source root and .. cannot escape it. Use -0 for NUL-delimited lists.

options.help: list source entries; do not transfer or change DEST
options.detail: Lists sources and leaves DEST untouched. A single source argument with no DEST lists it too.

options.help: preserve extended attributes (twice includes rsync internals)
options.detail: -XX also copies rsync-internal attributes. Whole-directory clones are disabled so each entry is handled individually. Large values spill to a temporary file beyond an 8 MiB in-memory budget.

options.help: preserve hard links within the transferred tree
options.detail: Preserves link groups among selected files, including across directories. Links to files outside the selection are not recreated.

options.help: create holes for zero-filled file regions
options.detail: Disables cloning. Works with delta, resumed and in-place writes.

options.help: reuse unchanged files from a previous snapshot
options.detail: Up to 20 directories. Relative paths start at the destination directory. Unchanged files with matching requested metadata become hard links; others are copied, and a snapshot can still serve as their delta basis.

options.help: copy symlinks as symlinks
skip symlinks that point outside the transfer tree
options.detail: Skips links that point outside the transfer tree and protects their existing destination entries from deletion.

options.help: transform symlink into referent file/dir
options.detail: Overrides -l. Metadata options such as -A and --fileflags then apply to the referent.

options.help: preserve permissions
change incoming file/directory permissions
options.detail: Numeric modes or comma-separated symbolic rules; D/F restrict a rule to directories or files, and repeated options append rules. Disables whole-directory clones. Works with protocol-3 helpers, because it changes existing mode fields.

options.help: preserve executability of regular files
options.detail: Only matters when --perms is off. Apple’s system rsync uses -E for extended attributes; use the long name when fallback must be unambiguous.

options.help: preserve BSD file flags (macOS)
options.detail: Adds a twelfth change-code character. On Linux the option is refused natively; fallback then needs an rsync built with --fileflags, which standard upstream builds are not.

options.help: preserve owner (super-user only)
options.detail: Names map between hosts unless --numeric-ids is set; the name mapping needs the helper feature.

options.help: preserve group
change destination owner/group (names or IDs)
options.detail: Names resolve on the destination host. Either field may be omitted. On a push, overrides still apply after a later --no-owner/--no-group.

options.help: same as --devices --specials
options.detail: Device nodes need privilege on the receiver. --no-D turns both off.

options.help: preserve ACLs (implies --perms)
options.detail: Remote ACLs need matching styles: macOS to macOS, or Linux to Linux. A macOS ↔ Linux request delegates before any write, and rsync itself rejects the tested cross-platform ACLs. Principals map by name unless --numeric-ids.

options.help: preserve modification times
preserve file access times (twice enables --open-noatime)
options.detail: Files and special inodes only; directories and symlinks keep rsync’s omission. -UU also requests O_NOATIME reads.

options.help: preserve creation times (macOS)
options.detail: Including directories and symlinks. On Linux the option is refused and handed to rsync.

options.help: avoid read access-time updates where supported
options.detail: May need file ownership or privilege. macOS ignores the flag.

options.help: omit directory modification/access/creation times
omit symlink modification/access/creation times
perform a trial run with no changes made
options.detail: Always ends with would transfer N files (X), delete M on stdout, even without -v.

options.help: send the whole file; disable resume and block matching
options.detail: Disables both verified-prefix resume and block matching, locally and remotely.

options.help: enable verified-prefix resume again
don't cross filesystem boundaries
specify the remote shell to use
options.detail: Precedence: -e, then XSYNC_RSH, then RSYNC_RSH, then a shell in XSYNC_OPTS, then config, then ssh.

options.help: specify the xs to run on the remote machine
options.detail: Bypasses the automatic helper lookup. The same command is kept if the transfer falls back, so it must then accept rsync’s server arguments too.

options.help: fail instead of re-executing rsync for missing support
options.detail: An option xs does not implement then exits 1; a helper missing a needed feature exits 4; a missing helper exits 127.

options.help: enable fallback (overrides XSYNC_FALLBACK=0)
skip creating new files on receiver
skip updating files that exist on receiver
delete extraneous files from dest dirs
options.detail: Also accepted: --del/--delete-during, --delete-before, --delete-delay and --delete-after. Source I/O errors suppress deletion unless --ignore-errors.

options.help: scan deletions and merge files after transfer
options.detail: Scans the destination after transfers finish and reloads receiver merge files from the updated tree.

options.help: omit empty directory chains from the file list
options.detail: Protected empty directories and their ancestors are kept.

options.help: also delete excluded files from dest dirs
options.detail: Makes unqualified include/exclude rules sender-only. Explicit receiver rules still protect entries.

options.help: delete even when the sender encountered I/O errors
delete at most NUM entries (exit 25 if exceeded)
force deletion of dirs even if not empty
don't transfer any file larger than SIZE
options.detail: Sizes accept K/M/G/T (binary) and KB/MB/GB/TB (decimal) suffixes.

options.help: don't transfer any file smaller than SIZE
options.detail: Same size syntax as --max-size.

options.help: limit bytes sent/copied per second (bare RATE: KiB/s)
options.detail: Bare numbers are KiB/s; suffixes K–P, KiB/MiB or decimal KB/MB are accepted and rounded to the nearest KiB/s. Zero disables the limit; nonzero rates below 512 bytes/s are rejected. Remote writers limit bytes after compression; local workers share one limit on bytes written, which disables APFS cloning.

options.help: remote idle I/O timeout (0 disables; exits with code 30)
options.detail: Integer seconds. Covers shell and handshake waits, partial frames, blocked writes and a helper that stays alive after the protocol ends. Keep-alives are sent at most every 10 seconds, or a third of the timeout.

options.help: keep partially transferred files
options.detail: Current helpers verify an existing destination prefix with XXH3-128 on both sides and send only the rest. Files up to 512 KiB use the whole-file path.

options.help: update destination files in-place
options.detail: Writes destination files directly. A delta basis is snapshotted so moved blocks are preserved while the original inode is updated.

options.help: create the destination's path component
don't map uid/gid values by user/group name
skip files that are newer on the receiver
don't skip files that match size and time
skip files that match in size
set the accuracy for mod-time comparisons
compress file data during the transfer (zstd)
options.detail: zstd, decompressed on several threads. Has no effect on local copies. A helper without compression support silently gets plain data. --compress-choice accepts only zstd or none.

options.help: explicitly set compression level
add a file-filtering RULE
options.detail: Supports +/-, H/S, P/R, !, merge rules, and the modifiers ! / s r p x. Plain include/exclude rules work with any helper; side, merge and CVS rules need the corresponding features.

options.help: merge .rsync-filter files (twice also excludes them)
options.detail: Same as --filter=': /.rsync-filter', including ancestor files. -FF also excludes the filter files.

options.help: exclude CVS defaults and .cvsignore patterns
options.detail: Adds per-directory .cvsignore files, built-in CVS exclusions, $HOME/.cvsignore and CVSIGNORE after explicit rules.

options.help: exclude files matching PATTERN
read exclude patterns from FILE
don't exclude files matching PATTERN
read include patterns from FILE
use NUL delimiters in list and filter merge files
options.detail: Applies to file lists, include/exclude files and merge files opened after the option. --no-from0 restores line mode.

options.help: give some file-transfer stats
use 1000-based units (-hh uses 1024)
options.detail: One rule everywhere: decimal units by default and with -h, binary with -hh. --no-h removes digit separators. JSON counters are never scaled.

options.help: show progress (default on terminals), or JSON events
options.detail: On by default when stderr is a terminal. On a pipe, plain --progress prints one line per second; --info=progress2 prints rsync’s line shape; --progress=json prints events.

options.help: suppress progress; XSYNC_PROGRESS=0 also disables it
same as --partial --progress
output a change-summary for all updates
retain high bytes in names; escape unsafe control bytes
file lines: %i %n %L %l %o %f %b %t %% (optional width)
append the same stdout stream to FILE
print the version, or this help, and exit
paths always travel as protocol data, not shell text
transport polling handles either pipe mode internally
no daemon transport or daemon greeting exists
explicitly install the matching release at ~/.local/bin refuses newer versions unless --force is supplied
options.detail: Never part of a transfer. Release files are found beside the executable, in a sibling dist/, in ../share/xs/releases/, or in XSYNC_RELEASE_DIR. An interrupted upload leaves the previous executable in place.

options.help: number of worker threads (default: performance cores)
always copy file data, even where a copy-on-write clone (APFS, same volume, with -pt) would be possible
options.detail: Clones only happen on the same APFS volume with at least -pt. They can carry xattrs, ACLs and access/creation times that -a alone would not copy.

options.help: create new files via temp file + rename (default)
create new byte-copied files directly (fewer renames; a crash can leave truncated files under final names)

unlisted.name: --delete-delay
unlisted.help: find deletions during the transfer, delete afterwards

unlisted.name: --info
unlisted.help: progress2, progress0, stats2 or stats0, comma separated

unlisted.name: --no-OPTION
unlisted.help: turn off a flag, for example --no-perms, --no-times, --no-D
